## What's the IRW?

The [Item Response Warehouse](index.qmd) is a free, open collection of harmonized item response data: more than 8,600 datasets and over 6.6 billion responses from education, psychology and beyond, all in one format and ready to pull straight into R or Python.

## Two tracks

```{=html}
<div class="hk">
<div class="hk-tracks">
  <section class="hk-track academic">
    <header><div class="k">Track 1</div><h3>Academic</h3></header>
    <div class="body">
      <p>Write a short, original research paper using IRW's vast reservoir of psychometric data.</p>
      <p><strong>Leave with a paper, working code, and the opportunity to co-author with GSE faculty.</strong></p>
    </div>
  </section>
  <section class="hk-track entre">
    <header><div class="k">Track 2</div><h3>Entrepreneurial</h3></header>
    <div class="body">
      <p>Build an open-science project, a site, or a startup using IRW's data architecture for any field beyond education.</p>
      <p><strong>Walk out with a new MVP and the opportunity to demo to a panel of investors and VC-backed entrepreneurs.</strong></p>
    </div>
  </section>
</div>
</div>
```

## Get ready

You don't need to know the IRW before you arrive, but an hour with these will put you ahead:

- [Getting started](getstarted.qmd): install the R or Python package and pull your first table.
- [Browse the data](data.qmd): filter the warehouse by size, construct, field and response type.
- [The core standard](standard.qmd): the one format every table shares, and the pattern the entrepreneurial track can borrow for other fields.
- [Using an AI assistant](agents.qmd): point your assistant at the warehouse.
- [Vignettes](vignettes/index.qmd): worked analyses across many datasets at once, for ideas about what a paper might look like.

## Questions?

Email [bdomingue@stanford.edu](mailto:bdomingue@stanford.edu). Code and data processing for the IRW are on [GitHub](https://github.com/itemresponsewarehouse).
